- **J03.90 (Acute tonsillitis, unspecified):** The provider's assessment is "acute tonsillitis." The note says this is her first episode, so the non-recurrent code applies.
- **Not J03.00 (Acute streptococcal tonsillitis):** The positive rapid strep test was recorded by the nurse. The provider never names strep as the cause. Coding rules do not allow a diagnosis to be taken from a test result alone, even though amoxicillin suggests the provider may have considered it. If the provider adds an addendum stating the cause is streptococcal, J03.00 would replace J03.90.
- **Fever not coded separately:** Fever is an expected part of acute tonsillitis.
- **No external cause code:** This is an infection, not an injury or other external event.

The assessment documents "Hepatitis C" without stating whether it is acute or chronic. In the ICD-10-CM Index, "Hepatitis, C" with no further description leads to B19.20 (unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma). The note does point toward chronic infection: antibody positive since 2019 and RNA still detectable now. Even so, a coder cannot assign chronicity from test results alone. Chronic hepatitis C (B18.2) needs the provider to document "chronic", which would normally prompt a query.

No external cause codes apply. A code for long-term drug therapy is not reported because treatment is only being started at this visit.

```json
["B19.20"]
```

Assign one code: H53.131 (sudden visual loss, right eye).

- **Why not central retinal artery occlusion:** This is an outpatient eye clinic visit. The assessment says the findings are "compatible with" central retinal artery occlusion. In the outpatient setting, that wording is treated as an uncertain diagnosis, so the occlusion is not coded as confirmed. Instead, code the documented sign, which is the sudden loss of vision in the right eye.
- **Why the retinal findings are not coded separately:** The whitened retina, cherry-red spot and narrowed arterioles are exam findings supporting the visual loss. A code for changes in retinal vascular appearance, right eye (H35.011), could arguably be added, but I did not include it.
- **No external cause codes:** No injury or external cause is documented.

The visit is coded to the provider's assessment only.

- **M76.62** (Achilles tendinitis, left leg) is the first-listed and only code.
- **No adverse-effect code is added.** The note mentions a recent levofloxacin course, but the provider never says the drug caused the tendinitis. A coder cannot assume that link, so T36.8X5A (adverse effect of other systemic antibiotics) is not assigned.
- **No external cause code applies.** There was no injury.
- **No long-term antibiotic use code applies.** The course finished six days ago.
